Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Thanks again for the call today — great conversation, Samantha and Tom. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can size Dedicated capacity properly.

Recap of what I heard from the discovery:
- Primary use: in-product chat and personalized responses for lending workflows.
- Latency target: p95 & p99 goals (~100-200ms p95 for short chats) — you called out user-facing latency as high priority.
- Security/regulatory: prefer Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) today; may evaluate Private (VPC/on-prem) later for specific regulated workloads.

Clarifying items needed to produce a preliminary GPU sizing:
1) Sustained TPS (requests/sec) and expected peak TPS (bursts).
2) Typical concurrency (how many overlapping user requests at peak).
3) Average token mix: avg input tokens / avg output tokens, and percent of requests that are short vs long.
4) Which model family you expect to run (e.g., Llama2-70B, Mistral-large, or a smaller curated model).

Preliminary notes/suggestions (subject to numbers above):
- For low-latency chat at scale we typically recommend H100-80GB for large 70B-class models, or A100-80GB as a cost-effective alternative; quantized 4-bit variants can dramatically reduce GPU memory and increase throughput if quality is acceptable.
- Key knobs: batching window, max concurrency per worker, KV cache reuse, and prefix caching for repeated system prompts.

Next steps: can you confirm the numbers above (1-3)? If easier, upload the spreadsheet with daytime peak hours — I can share with our SRE/solutions team for a quick sizing. Once we have those values, Marissa will produce a recommended Dedicated pool + autoscale plan and an estimated price range.

Thanks — I’ll hold off on formal sizing until we get that data.

—

Thanks Rafael — appreciate the recap. Couple answers below and I attached a quick spreadsheet (finova-prod-tps-estimate.xlsx) with hourly peaks for last 30 days.

Numbers:
- Sustained TPS: ~300 requests/sec during core business hours (US morning through early afternoon).
- Peak burst TPS: up to ~700 requests/sec for short spikes (few minutes).
- Peak concurrency: roughly 1,200 concurrent active sessions at absolute peak.
- Token mix (avg): input ~30 tokens, output ~200 tokens; about 80% of requests are chat-style Q&A (short-ish), 20% are long-generation (reports) that can go up to 1,500 output tokens but are <5% of total volume.
- Model: evaluating a 70B-class open model (we're testing Llama2-70B and a quantized Mistral variant).

We prefer Dedicated capacity to start — isolation and predictable throughput matter. We may move specific regulated flows to Private later.

Please let us know recommended GPU mix and if you need any more telemetry from our side.

Thanks — saw the spreadsheet. Initial sizing notes below (ballpark numbers for a 70B-class model):

Option A (performance / latency prioritized):
- 6 x H100-80GB (dedicated pool) with 2x hot-standby nodes for fast autoscale.
- Per-node config: limit worker concurrency to ~96 small-chat requests; use small batching window (5-10ms) to preserve latency.
- Estimated sustainable TPS (chat mix): ~350 TPS with room to handle bursts to ~700 using autoscale + pre-warmed standbys; p95 target ~120ms for 30in/200out median.
- Pros: best latency and headroom for long-tail requests; supports mixed workload.
- Cons: higher monthly infra cost.

Option B (cost-optimized):
- 8 x A100-80GB (or 10 x A100 depending on model/quantization) with slightly higher batching and tuned quantized weights.
- Estimated sustainable TPS: ~300 TPS; burst to 600 with autoscale. p95 ~150-220ms depending on quantization quality.

Optimization notes / recommendations:
- Encourage Finova to adopt 4-bit quantization for non-regulated flows — big throughput gains.
- Use prefix caching for repeated system prompts and a small KV cache window for multi-turn sessions to reduce token compute.
- Configure canary rollout with 10% traffic on the new Dedicated pool before full cutover.

Next actions: Rafael — I can draft a one-page sizing proposal (redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf) with recommended config, estimated monthly infra, and recommended rollout steps. Also need to confirm whether they require KMS/HSM integration + VPC peering for the Dedicated control plane.

—

Hi Samantha / Tom — thanks for the quick data. Attaching a short proposal (redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf) with the recommended configuration and next steps. Summary below:

Recommendation (short):
- Start with Option A: 6 x H100-80GB Dedicated pool + 2 pre-warmed standbys. Expected sustainable throughput for your chat mix ~350 TPS with autoscale headroom to 700 for spikes. Concurrency configured to meet your 1,200 peak sessions using multiple worker shards + prefix caching.

Why this fit:
- Balances low p99/p95 latency for user-facing chat while providing headroom for long-generation tails.

Follow-up items / ask from Finova:
1) Confirm: KMS/HSM required for keys? Do you need Private control plane or is Dedicated (Redwood-managed control plane + customer VPC peering) sufficient for now?
2) Approve a 30-45 minute call next week with Marissa + our SRE team to finalize node counts, autoscale policies, and rollout plan. Please propose a couple of times.
3) If ok, we’ll send a draft SOW and pricing range to procurement for review.

Attachments included: redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf (high-level config + cost ranges), finova-prod-tps-estimate.xlsx (their telemetry).

If that sounds good I’ll schedule the SRE call and loop procurement.
